#3214. Arcos Dorados (ARCO) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Digital growth surged, but wage pressure weighed on margins this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Arcos Dorados Holdings Inc. (ARCO +0.86%) reported top-line growth and expanded its market share position across Latin America despite a cautious consumer spending environment. Management announced a new capital allocation framework that includes the introduction of a share repurchase program and a focus on high-return capital expenditures. The company stated that digital penetration and loyalty program adoption continue to serve as primary growth drivers, with digital sales now comprising a majority of total system-wide revenue. Management also emphasized ongoing cost discipline and restructuring efforts intended to mitigate inflationary pressures in labor and food costs.

Daniel Schleiniger: Good morning, and thank you for joining Arcos Dorados' Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Webcast. With us today are Luis Raganato, our Chief Executive Officer; and Mariano Tannenbaum, our Chief Financial Officer. Today's webcast, which is being recorded, will consist of prepared remarks from our leadership team, which will be accompanied by a slide presentation that is also available in the Investors section of our website, ir.arcosdorados.com. To better follow the presentation, please note that you can set your view to full screen on the webcast platform. [Operator Instructions] After we conclude our opening remarks, we will answer your questions.

Today's call will contain forward-looking statements, and I refer you to the forward-looking statements section of our earnings release and recent filings with the SEC. We assume no obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements to reflect new or changed events or circumstances. In addition to reporting financial results in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, we report certain non-GAAP financial results. Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial results as compared with GAAP results, which can be found in today's earnings press release and conference call presentation as well as the unaudited financial statements filed today with the SEC on Form 6-K.

Following our customary format, today, Luis will present the highlights of the third quarter's consolidated results. Then he will review the main marketing and digital activities during the quarter as well as divisional revenue performance. Mariano will take you through consolidated and divisional profitability in addition to our main leverage metrics, restaurant growth and capital expenditures. Luis will then provide some final thoughts before opening the call for questions. Luis, over to you.

Luis Raganato: Thank you, Dan, and good morning, everyone. A few weeks ago, we held our 2026 Investor Day. During the presentation, we talked about the key success of the last several years, demonstrating how we strengthened the brand, captured significant market share, delivered strong revenue growth and more than doubled U.S. dollar EBITDA from 2019 to 2025. In other words, today, we are operating at a very high level in the region's QSR industry. We then took you through some of the initiatives we're working on for tomorrow and the key drivers we expect to sustain long-term growth. Marketing and digital, leveraging our strengths and connecting with guests when and where they want.

Innovation and technology, providing new ways to drive results and unlocking efficiencies across the business, development and supply chain, achieving higher returns on investment and building resilience into the operation. Our long-term growth objectives are ambitious, mid- to high single-digit annual total revenue growth, high single to low double-digit annual adjusted EBITDA growth, 550 to 600 restaurant openings from 2027 to 2030, and $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion in total capital expenditures from 2027 to 2030. We believe these objectives demonstrate the confidence we have in the business model and in the initiatives we are pursuing to capture this potential. Importantly, meeting these objectives implies additional free cash flow generation.

So today, I want to provide you with a clear view of our capital allocation framework. First, capital expenditures. We have a significant growth opportunity in a highly underpenetrated region. Importantly, we updated our development model to reduce the average investment per new restaurant without sacrificing sales and cash flow, which is already improving first year returns by 3 to 5 percentage points. Together with ongoing investments in modernization and technology, we believe this makes disciplined, high expected return CapEx, the best way to generate long-term shareholder value. Second, a healthy balance sheet.

That is where we are today with net debt to adjusted EBITDA of just 1.3x and an investment-grade debt rating, which will help us support the business through all operating environments. Third, dividends. We have a demonstrated history of paying a cash dividend whenever free cash flow generation allows and/or financial leverage remains at healthy levels. In every year since 2022, we paid an equal or larger dividend versus the prior year. Fourth, share repurchases. Today, we are announcing that the Board of Directors has approved the second share repurchase program in the company's history. We believe our stock is undervalued at current levels.

We are confident in our long-term plan and at current prices, we consider this to be an accretive investment opportunity. With that, we have been authorized to repurchase and cancel up to $25 million of Class A Arcos Dorados stock in the open market over the next 6 months. Let's turn to the results for the third quarter of 2026. Our third quarter results show that the business model continues to deliver in a demanding consumer environment. We grew the top line, protected underlying profitability, expanding our market share, and generated significantly more cash than a year ago. That combination is what allows us to keep funding growth and at the same time, return more capital to our shareholders.

Total revenue reached $1.3 billion, up more than 11% versus the prior year quarter in U.S. dollars in a period marked by generally challenging consumer dynamics. System-wide comparable sales grew 15.5%, driven by higher average check and positive guest traffic. New restaurants also contributed. We ended the quarter with more than 100 additional locations compared with a year ago. Underlying adjusted EBITDA rose 9% in U.S. dollars versus the prior year quarter, excluding the net impact of the significant federal tax credit in Brazil last year. Market share and digital sales penetration remained strong in the period, while revenue growth was strongest in Brazil and SLAD.

Based on our research, the McDonald's brand continues to command the highest market share across Latin America's QSR industry, almost double the nearest competitor. Even with this significant advantage, we were still able to expand market share in the region over the first 9 months of 2026. Market share measured by guest traffic was solid in all main markets during the period. Sales through digital channels grew by about 22% year-over-year and generated about 2/3 of total system-wide sales. This included very strong growth in NOLAD, where about half of system-wide sales are now generated through digital channels. Identified sales reached a new high of 29% of total sales.

Loyalty program membership grew by 60% versus the prior year with almost 38 million registered users. As shown at our Investor Day, this is the largest loyalty program in the region. Mobile Order & Pay, Delivery and Loyalty sales all remain strong, supported by increasing guest adoption across markets. Marketing campaigns included the Best Burger launch in several SLAD markets. This initiative was geared towards improving taste and quality perceptions in our core beef menu items as it brings tangible improvements in the way they are prepared, delivering hotter, juicier and tastier hamburgers. We maintained our value platform strategy across all key markets where consumers remain cautious with their spending.

These platforms offer guests a meal at an attractive price point of less than $5 and a choice between chicken or beef menu items, giving the brand a stronger presence in both categories. We also ran a campaign in the fish category with the reintroduction of the popular McFish sandwich in Brazil. From time to time, we make this guest favorite available for a limited time and this year was the best ever in terms of units sold. We drove brand affinity by turning the trend among Gen Z consumers by executing a region-wide program with Demon Hunters.

The program was built around the themed menu, which included iconic Chicken McNuggets with unique sauces plus a crafted beverage to deliver an exclusive experience to guests. Finally, as the Formula 1 circuit comes to Latin America with races in Mexico and Brazil, we introduced a Formula One meal across the region. It includes a limited edition Quarter Pounder with Cheese sandwich together with a collectible Formula 1 car, a crafted beverage in collaboration with Red Bull Racing and a unique Formula 1 McFlurry in partnership with Nestle's KitKat. In Mexico and Argentina, the program further leveraged sponsorships of popular local drivers, Checo Perez and Franco Colapinto, respectively.

In Brazil, comparable sales grew 3.5% with positive momentum in guest traffic growth. Together with 70 more restaurants than a year ago and a stronger real, this drove U.S. dollar revenue growth of more than 15%. NOLAD's comparable sales were about flat, an improvement versus the second quarter. Consumers in the division remain cautious, so we kept value platforms at the center of our marketing strategy. Panama, Martinique and French Guiana delivered encouraging comparable sales growth and a stronger Mexican peso helped U.S. dollar revenue grow almost 8% in the quarter. And while Argentina and Venezuela continue to drive SLAD comparable sales growth, markets such as Colombia, Peru and Uruguay also had solid third quarter top line performance.

Mariano Tannenbaum: Thanks, Luis. Good morning, everyone. In our analysis today, we will make an adjustment to reported results to more accurately evaluate underlying EBITDA performance. The adjustment is the net federal tax credit we recognized in Brazil in the third quarter of last year, which added $85.6 million to that quarter's adjusted EBITDA. Including it will distort the year-over-year comparison. So when I refer to underlying growth or margins today, I am excluding that effect. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $125.9 million with a 9.5% consolidated margins. Both food and paper and G&A supported consolidated margins in the period.

Better pricing and product mix, together with proactive initiatives by the supply chain team, drove a 90 basis point improvement in food and paper as a percentage of revenues. All 3 divisions contributed to the result, which was the third consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion. G&A rose well below blended inflation due to the restructuring we implemented starting at the end of last year. These positive margin impacts were offset by higher payroll and occupancy and other operating expenses as a percentage of total revenues. All 3 divisions experienced modest labor cost pressures, especially SLAD, while both Brazil and NOLAD saw some fixed cost deleveraging versus the prior year.

Brazil's adjusted EBITDA grew by about 10% in U.S. dollars versus the prior year. Modest payroll cost pressure, together with some higher fixed costs, accounted for most of the margin pressure compared with last year. Importantly, food and paper was lower as a percentage of revenue versus last year, which is a sign that we are building sales the right way. NOLAD's adjusted EBITDA grew nearly double digits with margin expansion of 20 basis points, demonstrating the effectiveness of our value platforms at protecting margins in a challenging consumer environment. I am encouraged by the results of our efforts to rebalance volume and average check growth to rebuild NOLAD's margin over time.

In SLAD, improved food and paper performance was offset by payroll cost pressures, keeping the division's adjusted EBITDA margin about flat versus last year. As a result, adjusted EBITDA growth remained in line with revenue growth in U.S. dollars, up high single digits versus last year. Turning to the bottom line. Net income attributable to Arcos Dorados was $31.2 million or $0.15 per share. Excluding last year's federal tax credit, net income grew almost 24% and net income margin expanded 20 basis points to 2.3%. This growth came from our underlying operating performance and the lower income tax expense versus the prior year.

As Luis explained, expanding our restaurant footprint while maintaining a modernized portfolio is a strategic decision we believe will generate long-term shareholder value. Next, we must maintain a strong balance sheet to grow consistently over time while ensuring our ability to navigate the region's macroeconomic cycles. During the third quarter, we deployed more than $70 million in capital expenditures, bringing the total investment through the first 9 months of the year to $156 million. These investments included 35 restaurant openings in the quarter and 70 openings through the first 3 quarters of the year.

Returns on investment continued to improve and the remaining restaurants needed to meet this year's opening target have either already been opened or are currently under construction. We constantly seek to enhance our capital structure and debt profile. As of the end of September, our net debt was about in line with the end of 2025, and the net leverage ratio ended the third quarter at a healthy 1.3x. We continue to be encouraged by the trends we are seeing in adjusted free cash flow generation, which was more than $100 million higher in the last 12 months versus the prior comparable period. As I just showed you, our top 2 capital allocation priorities are in great shape.

This is why we are able to reinforce our belief in providing shareholders with additional sources of return, such as our track record of increasing our dividend and today's announcement of a share repurchase program. We follow a disciplined approach to capital allocation so that we can focus on what we do best, delivering great food and experiences to our guests. It is important to remember that the long-term ambition we shared at our Investor Day reflects an average growth trend over the long term and it's not specific guidance for any single year. It is also macro-neutral, meaning it does not assume any specific economic or political scenario.

We believe it is an ambitious, achievable level of growth based on our confidence in the business model's ability to deliver attractive returns and generate compelling shareholder value over time. Let me close by highlighting the main points of the third quarter. Total revenue grew more than 11% in U.S. dollars with system-wide comparable sales up 15.5%. Underlying adjusted EBITDA grew 9% with food and paper improving for the third consecutive quarter. Adjusted free cash flow for the last 12 months reached $156 million, about 3x the level of a year ago. And with a healthy balance sheet, we're adding a share repurchase program to our dividend track record to return more capital to our shareholders.

Luis Raganato: Thanks, Mariano. Let me share a few final thoughts before we take your questions. We had a solid third quarter with normalizing comparable sales trends in Brazil, which included some encouraging guest traffic trends as well. Importantly, underlying profitability in the quarter also performed well, rising high single digits versus last year. The fourth quarter is off to a solid start. Comparable sales trends continued normalizing in October, and we have some attractive marketing campaigns designed to take full advantage of the upcoming holiday season. We are finalizing our plan for next year, which includes more targeted marketing campaigns, strong partnerships throughout the year and exciting product launches designed to drive comparable sales growth.

Also, we believe there are margin opportunities through the implementation of the technologies and continued cost discipline that we talked about during our Investor Day. There is one word we want you to remember today, it is discipline, discipline in how we invest with a development model that is improving returns on new restaurants. Discipline in how we manage costs, which continues to generate G&A leverage and has improved food and paper for 3 consecutive quarters; and discipline in how we allocate capital, which today allows us to announce a share repurchase program while we keep investing for growth. Thank you for joining today's call. Dan, back to you to start the Q&A session.

Daniel Schleiniger: Thanks, Luis. We'll now take your questions. [Operator Instructions] Let's get started with Eric Huang from Santander. Eric sends us actually 4 questions, and so we'll just take them one at a time. The first one will be for you, Luis. We saw some sequential deceleration in Brazil's comp sales momentum. Could you elaborate a bit more on the trends throughout the quarter and perhaps how you're thinking about the sales trends as we head into 4Q '26 and 2027, especially given the more challenging consumer backdrop?

Luis Raganato: All right. Thank you very much, Eric, for the question. The second quarter had the boost of the World Cup actions. The good news is that during the third quarter, we kept on growing not only in volume, but in sales with still better margins. Your question has more inside of it, so it's more complex. So let me give you a little bit more detail about what happened during this third quarter. First, let me talk to you about the sector. The sector showed an increased traffic in the foodservice and the QSR segment.

And in this context, our team was able to sustain positive comp sales growth building on the momentum that we had generated in that second quarter. At the same time, comparable [indiscernible] volume, that volume growth was the strongest of the last 8 quarters, and it's allowed us to support a healthier sales performance. These results were supported by the continued execution of the local strategy, a strategy that began last year, a strategy that was based on the launch during this quarter of the second phase of [ Economequi ]. Economequi, just as a reminder, is our always on affordability platform, reinforcing the commitment that we have to be the most accessible option in the market.

And we complemented this platform with initiatives that were built around the passion points of our guests, activities like Happy Meal campaigns that included Spider-Man and SpongeBob. And we also appeal to Gen Z guests with the K-Pop Demon Hunters partnership. This initiative was a [indiscernible], we call that when these actions covered sandwiches, desserts and beverages. In beef, we also have news. We innovated with the launch of Brabo SmokeHouse in the premium category. And we also brought back the McFish sandwich that worked as a limited time offer and had the best campaign ever in terms of unit sales. So we boosted our sales with the action -- with all the World Cup actions in the second quarter.

Then with these actions, we are preparing the base with a healthy growth in sales for the fourth quarter. So the result of this strategy is that we grew traffic share even in the context of growing QSR industry volumes. We were able to keep -- we keep competing on our very strong position with more than double the share of the nearest competitor. I think it's worth highlighting how we grew because while the rest of the market relied more on aggressive promotional activity that we have and a heavy impact in gross margins, we took a more sustainable approach.

We try to balance price and volume, and we saw that our growth was driven by guests that came back to our restaurants, while at the same time, we managed to expand gross margin like I told you. So this is showing the effectiveness of our value proposition. So far in the fourth quarter, we are seeing that the evolution of volume and sales are in line with our expectations. We believe that consumers will remain cautious with tight household budgets, but we believe that the recovery in the industry traffic is an encouraging signal.

So we'll keep a disciplined approach with relevant brand experiences, competitive value, and great execution across all channels because our customers are omnichannel so that we can capture this demand profitably. Dan, back to you.

Daniel Schleiniger: Thanks, Luis. Eric's two other questions related -- also related to -- the 2 other questions related to Brazil, and I'm going to read them together for you, Mariano. On the cost side, and there's a lot in here, so bear with me. On the cost side, payroll was once again a headwind given that in Brazil, we should have the reduction in working hours. How should we think about this line, especially in 2027? And what are the main tools and initiatives that could offset such impacts?

And along the lines of reforms, this is labor reform, he also asked with the tax reform in Brazil, the VAC system introduction, what could be the main impacts in terms of profitability when we look at -- into 2027?

Mariano Tannenbaum: Perfect. Good morning, everybody, and thanks, Eric, for the question. I will start first discussing about payroll in general, and then I'll go to the specific of Brazil that you are asking. In terms of payroll efficiency, it has steadily improved across our markets over the past several years. You remember before the pandemic, what our figures were and how they improved about 200 basis points in the last years. So -- and that's the evolution over the last years. During this quarter, wage inflation run ahead of average check growth in all 3 divisions. We are seeing that performance in the 3 divisions.

And as a result, payroll expenses slightly increased as a percentage of revenues if we compare to the prior year. But that said, we continue to mitigate part of this pressure through productivity initiatives, improved scheduling accuracy, and also using digital tools that enhance labor deployment across our restaurants. So while payroll was a headwind during the quarter, we believe the underlying dynamics are improving, and that's worth mentioning. And we have already started to see encouraging trends and expect payroll performance to improve sequentially during the fourth quarter of 2026 as sales growth provides greater leverage on fixed costs, and all the productivity initiatives I mentioned continue to deliver results.

Taken together for 2026, these improving trends give us confidence that if you look at the full year, payroll costs as a percentage of revenues will remain broadly in line with 2025. Now going to the specifics about labor reform in Brazil. Well, we are closely monitoring the change in legislation in Brazil. There were several changes in the last couple of months. And once the regulation is final, then we will be able to determine its operational and financial impacts. We have experience managing evolving labor environments, including learnings from other markets. We operate in 20 different markets with 20 different labor regulations and laws.

And -- where we already -- we operate in those markets with the type of schedule that Brazil is moving to, and we will implement those initiatives in -- when we manage the Brazilian market. Our scheduling tools, productivity initiatives, operational flexibility, they will give us the levers to mitigate the potential pressures that while maintaining service quality and a good experience for our crews and guests at our restaurants. The last question was related to the Brazilian tax reform. And in this case, the government is now adding regulations to the new tax reform laws. With that, I think it would be premature to quantify the scope and depth of the impact.

Our understanding is that the restaurant sector will receive a lower VAT rate than was approved for the general legislation. Additionally, this new VAT tax regime will apply to the entire economy, not just the QSR industry. And the tax reform will be implemented over a transition period, that's important to mention, during which the current tax laws are phased out and the new VAT regime is phased in over the course of several years.

Daniel Schleiniger: Thanks, Mariano. [Indiscernible] with Eric, but we'll move to NOLAD. Eric's last question is, similar to what he asked with sales trends in Brazil, if you could walk us through the main trends in NOLAD, especially with regard to Mexico, that would be helpful. So that one to you, Luis.

Luis Raganato: Thank you very much, Eric, again. Yes, let me start with NOLAD, then I go to the specifics in Mexico. In NOLAD, in general, we saw continued pressure on consumer spending. Traffic was slightly down in the sector, and we saw also a highly competitive environment. But despite that, and this happened across the markets, the division maintained a stable performance during the quarter. The main focus was on the value strategy that together with the strength of our brand, and I would say, the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives, we were able to maintain our strong leadership position. The sales increase was driven more from volume than from average check.

And regarding channels, the strongest ones were delivery and service centers. In particular, in Mexico, we have seen a more challenging operating environment in this last quarter, especially in the retail sector, which has been impacted by continued pressure on consumer spending, and this was generated mainly on families' disposable income. However, the food service sector showed resilience. We managed to outperform both the food service sector and the QSR segment, even with positive comparable value. So that's great news. And as a result of that, we were able to gain market share.

It was very important to maintain the focus on value and combined with the strength again of the McDonald's brand and relevant marketing initiatives because that is what helped us not only maintain the value share, but the visit share also. So those marketing initiatives were the K-Pop Demon Hunters menu, coupled with our value platform that in Mexico is called [ Elige tu Fav ], and the continued growth of our Loyalty program. Digital sales are increasing in Mexico in a very healthy way also. And of course, all here to support top line growth and keep brand perception very strong. That is very important for us in the long term.

Sales mostly were driven by volume with a notable improvement in gross margin. So looking ahead, we remain confident in the fundamentals of our business and in the ability to capture demand supported by the solid marketing plan and strong operational execution. Dan?

Daniel Schleiniger: Thanks, Luis. I'll stay with you, Luis. A question from Jonathan Schwartz from ION Group. And he asks, have you noticed any increase in traffic in Brazil since the ban of online betting in late September?

Luis Raganato: All right. Thank you, Jonathan, for the question. Now I would say that it's too early to say if the market or even the sector has had any impact. But we think that the banning was a provisional measure. And looking to 2027, if this remains or becomes permanent, then we could see families resume a higher degree of spending on eating out and other forms of entertainment.

Daniel Schleiniger: Great. Thanks, Luis. We'll move now to Melissa Byun from Bank of America. She has a couple of questions that are very similar to questions from Alvaro Garcia at BTG Pactual. So I'll go through the questions first. And we'll start with you, Mariano. Melissa says, hello, can you comment on the margin outlook in Brazil given higher food costs and beef in particular, and also the new labor schedule 5 [indiscernible] labor schedule. What opportunities do you have to mitigate the pressure? Alvaro from BTG asked similar, can you give us more color on payroll and employee occupancy, other expenses in Brazil? So I think that's related to the margin question.

And can you comment on different strategy you have to address the work week reduction in Brazil over the next few years? I think you've already addressed the work week piece, but maybe you want to give a little more color on the margin piece.

Mariano Tannenbaum: Perfect. Thanks, Melissa and Alvaro, for the questions. Yes, I will go first for a margin update and outlook in Brazil, then go specifically about beef costs. Update, Brazil this quarter, the adjusted EBITDA grew $6.2 million up to $68.1 million in this quarter. This growth was supported by comp sales, new restaurant openings, better gross margin, leverage in G&A and the appreciation of the Brazilian real. Excluding the net federal tax credit, adjusted EBITDA margin contracted in the quarter by 60 basis points, mostly because of the phasing of some operating expenses, mainly outside services and other restaurant costs that landed in this quarter and are not recurrent, together with slightly higher payroll costs as a percentage of revenue.

When we look Brazil, year-to-date, what we observed is that EBITDA margin remains 50 basis points above the prior year, of course, excluding the tax credit, and we are very pleased with the performance of Brazil. Thinking -- well, in particular, I'm very pleased with the improvement we have seen in food and paper, driven by better pricing, our product mix together with supply chain initiatives. It's, I think, important to highlight that this marks our fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year food and paper improvement in Brazil. We also benefited from lower G&A following last year's restructuring that we talked about in previous quarters.

And going to the outlook, as Luis mentioned, the fourth quarter is off to a solid start in terms of sales. We continue to see food and paper and G&A as supportive. As I mentioned, as sales grow, we expect operating leverage to improve and some recurring -- some specific costs that we observed in the third quarter will not be there on the fourth quarter. So we are slightly positive, cautiously optimistic in the outlook for Brazil's margin for the next quarter and the beginning of next year. Going specifically about beef costs, it's true that in Brazil, the beef costs increased above inflation during 2026.

However, as I just mentioned, the impact was offset by more favorable trends across other food inputs and disciplined revenue management. So that's how we obtain a better food and paper during the last fourth quarter than we had back in 2025.

Daniel Schleiniger: Great. Thanks, Mariano. Melissa has switched now from Brazil to Mexico. The first part, I think she's already -- we've already answered, I'll read it anyway. And the second part we'll come back to you, Mariano. So the first part is, can you provide some additional color on sales in Mexico through the third and fourth quarters to date? I think Luis has addressed that. And then she asked about potential offsets to the minimum wage hike and shorter work week next year in Mexico. What impacts do you anticipate from the tax reform in Mexico? So we'll stick with you, Mariano.

Mariano Tannenbaum: Perfect. In terms of the minimum wage hike in Mexico, we have seen these type of increases in the last 4 to 5 years. And if you see the performance that we had in Mexico over those years was really encouraging in terms of EBITDA growth, in terms of sales growth. So in this respect, I don't think that we don't expect any material changes in our performance in Mexico given the hike in minimum wage. We think that this is a virtuous cycle where we see more disposable income.

We see that sales at our stores increase and that we are able to mitigate the impact of the payroll cost line by increasing sales and other efficiencies that we are gaining in that market. We are very pleased with the performance in Mexico with this in the last years, and we don't expect any changes given the impact on minimum wage. In terms of the tax reform in Mexico, we are also not seeing any material impact on a consolidated level at the income tax line in Arcos Dorados.

Daniel Schleiniger: Okay. Thanks, Mariano. Going to move now to Thiago Bortoluci from Goldman Sachs. Thiago has a couple of questions. To what would you attribute your recent relative growth performance versus the #2 operator in Brazil? That one is for you, Luis.

Luis Raganato: All right. Thank you, Thiago, for the question. I hope you're doing well. Okay. First, I can't speak about the specific competitor's performance, especially since we don't know how they calculate comparable sales. And we don't also -- we don't know how detailed -- we don't have the detailed financials to analyze. What I can tell you is that we believe we're building sales in a sustainable way. In the third quarter, we generated the best case volume growth of the last 8 quarters, while also expanding our gross margin. Evidence of this is that we have 2:1 market share advantage. And even so, we managed to grow this market share even more.

So what we observed was that most of our competitors are using aggressive promotional activity that is usually bad for margins and sustainable over time. And this is why we seek to balance price, volume, and channel growth thinking about the long term. Dan?

Daniel Schleiniger: Thanks, Luis. And Thiago's second question for you, Mariano. Could you please comment directionally on how gross margin and SG&A evolved per business unit?

Mariano Tannenbaum: Perfect. Thiago, we have seen improvements in food and paper in the 3 divisions. Brazil was the main contributor with food and paper costs showing a meaningful reduction compared to last year. In this case, the division benefited from lower chicken, potato, and ice cream costs, and the currency appreciation supporting gross margin recovery. In the case of SLAD also experienced a relevant decrease in food and paper costs, mainly because input cost inflation in Argentina and Chile remained below general inflation. And we also had a more profitable product mix in this case. And finally, NOLAD delivered further gains supported by lower costs, favorable product mix, and a more benign currency environment in Mexico, Costa Rica and Panama.

Our pricing strategy is worth mentioning remains disciplined and closely aligned with inflation. So with a pricing strategy aligned with inflation, we are seeing reduction in cost inputs, and we are very pleased with the results we have seen during this quarter. In terms of G&A, we are also seeing improvements in G&A in the 3 divisions. The 3 divisions after the restructuring process have a leaner and more agile cost structure and is better aligned with our strategic priorities and growth agenda. In this case, SG&A could be affected by appreciation of local currencies, but in constant currency and in real terms, we are seeing improvements in the 3 divisions.

Daniel Schleiniger: Okay. Thanks, Mariano. We have another question, and this one, I'm going to start again with you. And this is from Jorge Puszkar from JPMorgan. How does the election in Brazil change the expectations for system-wide sales in Brazil for the next 2 years? And maybe we can expand on how it impacts the business sort of overall.

Luis Raganato: Let me take the question because it's about sales and the business. Thank you for the question, Jorge. And we've been in Latin America for more than 40 years, almost 50 years in Brazil. And for us, we concentrate in the things that we can control. And we are very focused on our business. The political, economic and social environment is part of the environment that we have to manage. And so far, we don't see anything that could affect us in the near future. So we are very confident in our business model, and we'll keep our ambitions.

Daniel Schleiniger: Thanks, Luis. That was the last question in the queue. So we've reached the end of the Q&A session. Thanks again for your interest in Arcos Dorados and for joining today's webcast. Our next earnings call will be in the middle of March 2027, when we're going to report the results for the fourth quarter of 2026. Until then, we wish you all a very happy holiday season and start of the new year. Have a great day.

#3213. HubSpot brings back co-founder Brian Halligan as CEO to ‘refound’ it

Brian Halligan told Bloomberg he does not want HubSpot “swallowed up by a private equity firm”. Its shares have halved this year, and Adobe’s Karen Burgess will become finance chief.

HubSpot co-founder Brian Halligan is back as chief executive, five years after he stepped down. He replaces Yamini Rangan, who also leaves the board, with immediate effect from 12 November, the company announced. HubSpot calls it a “refounding” of the company.

Halligan told Bloomberg’s Brody Ford that he plans to overhaul HubSpot’s product, culture and sales processes.

“I don’t want to see HubSpot swallowed up by a private equity firm or shrink,” Halligan told Bloomberg. “I want to rebuild it and reimagine it.”

HubSpot’s shares had lost half their value this year through Wednesday, on slowing growth and fear of disruption from AI-native tools, Bloomberg reported. The company may have focused too much on short-term financial targets rather than great products, Halligan said.

“I don’t know if you looked at the last earnings, but the numbers aren’t great,” he told Bloomberg.

Halligan co-founded HubSpot in 2005 with Dharmesh Shah, its chief technology officer, and ran it for 16 years. He led it through its stock market listing to a market value of more than $30bn in 2021, the company said. He has sat on the board since 2005.

He stepped down as CEO in 2021 after a snowmobile accident, Kevin McLaughlin noted for The Information. Since then he has spent time at Sequoia Capital, including hosting its podcast, according to Bloomberg.

“This is a refounding, and I can’t wait to start!” Halligan said in the announcement.

Under Rangan, who took over in September 2021, HubSpot grew from 135,000 customers to more than 311,000. Revenue rose from $1.3bn in 2021 to an expected $3.7bn in 2026, according to the company. Rangan will stay until 1 December to hand over.

“Brian knows this company better than anyone, and I have tremendous confidence in his leadership as HubSpot enters its next chapter,” Rangan said.

HubSpot is also changing its chief financial officer. Kate Bueker will retire on 11 February 2027, which the company called long planned. Karen Burgess will replace her.

Burgess is chief financial officer of Adobe’s Creativity and Productivity unit, a $20bn business, and has been at Adobe since 2002. She joins HubSpot on 30 November and takes over as CFO in February.

Many software companies face a crisis of confidence about the AI era, Bloomberg reported. Adobe named a new CEO in September, and Workday has also changed its leadership. ServiceNow’s shares had their record 25% drop last month.

HubSpot said in October it would cut 660 jobs as it pivots to AI. On Thursday, it reaffirmed the guidance for the fourth quarter and full year it gave on 4 November.

#3212. Here’s Apple’s new ad for the holiday season, featuring MacBook Neo

The last few years of Apple holiday ads have revolved around iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods. For 2026, the new holiday film “The Dreamer” diverts from tradition and instead puts the spotlight on the Mac, specifically the MacBook Neo … although even the iPhone 3GS gets a cameo appearance.

In the ad, you see a child with a passion for art and drawing. As he grows up, though, a combination of self-consciousness and peer pressure means he hides his passions away.

The ad culminates with his parents gifting him as a teenager a new MacBook Neo, which he uses to animate his drawings into a cartoon.

you have to give it to them (or their PR/Ad agency) - they know how to produce emotional videos without becoming cheesy or too over the top. There's a lot of subtle little things that they do just perfectly. The underdog series was similarly brilliant.

In its description of the film, Apple says “sometimes all it takes to remember what makes us special, is someone who believes in us”.

As previously mentioned, the iPhone 3GS is briefly shown in a flashback sequence, and there’s a shot of a 2010-era iMac too.

This is a personal take, but it might be the company’s best in years.

#3210. Aya Gold & Silver (AYA) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Record quarterly output and Boumadine economics drive the story.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (AYA -6.66%) reported record quarterly results for the third quarter of 2026, characterized by significant increases in silver equivalent production and revenue. Management reported that the Zgounder Silver Mine has reached a stable production rate of approximately 6 million ounces per year, supported by record milling and mining throughput enabled by supplemental crushing capacity. The company has prioritized the development of the Boumadine project, where a preliminary economic assessment outlined substantial net present value and a 14-year mine life. Management stated that the company remains in a strong financial position with $183.8 million in cash, which will support the funding of future capital projects at Boumadine without immediate external financing needs. Furthermore, the company expanded its exploration footprint in Morocco by 50% through the acquisition of the Anti-Atlas and Tizi portfolios, broadening its exposure to precious and critical metals.

Operator: Good morning, everyone. I'll now turn the call over to Elisabeth Hamaoui, Aya Gold and Silver's Director of Corporate and Financial Communications. Please go ahead.

Elisabeth Hamaoui: Thank you, operator, and welcome to Aya's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Joining us today are Benoit La Salle, President and CEO; Ugo Landry-Tolszczuk, Chief Financial Officer; Elias, Chief Legal and Sustainability Officer; Raphael Beaudoin, Executive Vice President of Operations; and David Lalonde, Executive Vice President of Exploration. We will refer to a presentation available via the webcast and on our website as we will be making forward-looking statements during the call, please refer to the cautionary notes in the presentation, news release and MD&A as well as the risk factors in our annual information form.

Technical information in the presentation has been reviewed and approved by Raphael Beaudoin, Aya's Executive Vice President of Operations; and David Lalonde, Aya's Executive Vice President of Exploration, both qualified persons as defined under National Instrument 43-101 Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. And following the presentation, we will have a Q&A session. I would now like to turn the call over to Benoit La Salle. Benoit?

Benoit La Salle: Elisabeth, thank you. Welcome, everybody, to our Q3 2026 call. Q3 was another record quarter for Aya with Zgounder and the Boumadine reclaim operation each achieving the highest production to date. Our operation initiatives are paying off, delivering more scale, lower cash costs and solid cash flow. In the quarter, we've also provided you with an updated PEA on our Boumadine project, which was showing stronger economics and a longer mine life. Further, we also presented two acquisition where we've added new permits to the portfolio. So let me take you to the PowerPoint presentation that you have, Slide #5, as we do every quarter, just to review quickly the KPIs in the operation for the third quarter.

So if you go to Slide #5, you see that we had an excellent quarter where revenues are up 90% year-over-year from $54 million achieving this year -- this quarter in 2026, $103 million. This is kind of now a run rate, assuming good weather, obviously. We also have utilized a bulk shipment to ship the tailings to Asia, and that worked very, very well. And so we are on track to meet our guidance. On the right-hand side, you see that the silver equivalent production for the quarter was 536,000 ounces. Sales are at 492,000 ounces. So of course, there's always a little bit of lag between the shipment and the sale, but an extremely profitable operation. The realized price per ounce of silver equivalent is $34 because we do get a payability of 50%. Don't forget those are tailings with nasty elements and we're shipping them to Asia to a smelter.

On Slide #9, you see over the year of 2026, how cash has changed. We started the year with a cash position of $136 million.

So the PEA is done on three years of drilling. It's a Tier 1 asset. It's got fantastic economics because it's a low CapEx. We can build this project for less than $500 million. It has a payback, which is extremely quick. It's low risk because it's very simple, three payable concentrate, zinc, lead and pyrite. You recall, it's got 43% sulfur in the ore, which is what is needed for sulfuric acid. So it's a low-risk stand-alone model. We can fund this ourselves through equity that we have, so or through cash flow, I should say. So we can fund this through cash flow.

This after three years, we're starting construction. After seven years, it will be in operation, which normally is 20 years. So you have very strong economics, very low initial CapEx, fantastic capital efficiency ratio of 7.6%, and that is at the base case. #3209. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang set to be fired, with Johny Srouji among possible replacements [U]

Following reports of a potential second affair – this time with a subordinate – Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang looks certain to be fired by the company’s board, probably later today (though he may be allowed to ‘resign’). Apple’s chief hardware officer Johny Srouji has been listed among the potential replacements, though this seems unlikely.

Update: As we predicted, he’s gone today and Kress was indeed named interim CEO …

For anyone who’s been away from the planet for the past fortnight, Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy has been the main headline news in the tech press since it came to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days.

Things got even worse yesterday when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

It was already looking inevitable that he would be fired, and the latest revelation adds to the urgency. The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was meeting last night to discuss the CEO’s future. That future at Nvidia is likely to be measured in hours rather than days.

The board now needs to find a replacement, and Bloomberg provides a rundown on some of the potential candidates. CFO Colette Kress looks likely to head the list for at least an interim appointment. The paper names a number of other possibilities, including Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji.

Srouji has led one of the most successful in-house silicon programs in the industry, overseeing the custom chips that power the iPhone, Mac and other Apple devices. His track record gives him deep credibility on chip design, product integration and long-term technology roadmaps. But much of his experience has been built inside Apple’s tightly controlled ecosystem, and he hasn’t been tested in the kind of high-profile salesmanship which Huang is famous for.

Given the urgency, my money is on Nvidia announcing Kress as at least interim CEO, if not a permanent replacement. It seems exceedingly unlikely that Srouji would be appointed at this time, given the in-depth negotiations and discussions that would need to take place.

As to whether he’s a potential candidate following an interim appointment, it still seems unlikely. There was an earlier report of his claimed dissatisfaction at the company, but it seems a stretch to imagine him jumping ship so soon after his promotion to chief hardware officer.

#3208. Nebius shares fall 16% as data centre delays cut its 2026 outlook

Revenue rose to $980.8m and beat estimates, but delayed third-party sites push some sales into 2027. Nebius now plans to spend up to $45bn next year.

Arkady Volozh, founder and CEO of Nebius.

Nebius shares fell 16% on Thursday after the Amsterdam-based AI cloud company cut its outlook for this year. It also raised its spending plans, CNBC’s Jordan Novet reported. The fall came despite third-quarter revenue that rose 571% from a year earlier, to $980.8m.

Analysts surveyed by LSEG had expected $907.5m, according to CNBC. Nebius posted adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of $465.8m, against a loss of $5.2m a year earlier, its results show. Its net loss narrowed to $37.5m from $119.6m.

Nebius now expects 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3bn to $3.4bn range. Founder and chief executive Arkady Volozh gave the outlook in his letter to shareholders. Analysts had expected $3.37bn, CNBC reported. For 2027, Nebius expects revenue of $12bn to $13bn.

The cut comes from delays at data centre sites that Nebius rents from other companies. Some capacity due this year has moved to the first half of 2027. The contracts behind it remain in place, Deborah Sophia reported for Reuters.

One of them is a 300MW site in Vineland, New Jersey, held up by delays in power, John Reynolds reported for Tech.eu. Microsoft is a major customer there.

“Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now. We are not immune,” Volozh said, according to Tech.eu. “Customers have been kept informed and none of that capacity is cancelled.”

All of Nebius’s own sites under construction are on track or ahead of schedule, Volozh said, according to Reuters. He added that most of the next gigawatt Nebius brings online will be on its own sites.

Nebius now expects to spend about $27bn this year, up from its earlier forecast of $20bn to $25bn, CNBC reported. For 2027, it plans $40bn to $45bn, well above the $28.77bn analysts expected, according to FactSet data cited by CNBC.

Customer prepayments and asset-backed financing will cover 75% to 85% of next year’s spending, the company said. That financing rests on existing contracts with large customers such as Microsoft and Meta, according to Reuters.

“We have no doubt that this capacity will be sold. Clients are looking for capacity already for 2028, and prices for 2027 are going up. We do not see any risk,” chief financial officer Dado Alonso said, according to Reuters.

Nebius expects to break even on a pre-tax basis by the end of 2027. In October, it borrowed $3.5bn from Citi.

Thursday’s fall came on the day Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive. Nvidia held about $329m of Nebius shares at the end of June, CNBC reported, citing a filing.

Rival CoreWeave reported results that beat estimates on Tuesday, and ruled out new unsecured debt. Nebius had lost more than a third of its value in October, Reuters reported. Investors had questioned the cost of the AI build-out.

“The demand for AI is real and substantial. Everything else, like building the capacity and financing it, is just a task,” Volozh said on a call with analysts, according to CNBC.

#3207. 30% of iPhone Duo buyers may have returned it, but I don’t think Apple should worry

A poll of 9to5Mac readers who were lucky enough to take delivery of their iPhone Duo in the first few days shows that 30% of them have returned it for a refund.

While that could be considered bad news for the future of the device, I don’t personally consider it either surprising or worrying …

Following a report by The Verge on iPhone Duo buyers who opted to return the device for a refund within Apple’s 14-day “no questions asked” period, we thought it would be interesting to get a sense of how many people may have done this.

9to5Mac readers were always likely to have had their fingers hovering over the pre-order button for the best shot at taking early delivery, with the first of these having hit the end of the 14-day window. We ask those of you who fall into this category to tell us whether you kept or returned the device.

With close to 6,000 total votes, the results showed that close to a third of you returned your Duo.

For any other device, that would be a disastrous return rate. For the Duo, however, I don’t think it’s terribly surprising.

I voted to say I returned it just so I could see the results. I’ve never ordered nor returned an iPhone Duo.

Not providing a way to see the results without voting will have massively skewed the results. Even if the poll were better, this is a wild claim to draw from one specific, poorly assembled assembled poll.

As we noted yesterday, Apple described the iPhone Duo as “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original.” The size of that change shows up in a whole range of ways, from the weight of the device through the changed aspect ratio of the front display to a completely new way of using an iPhone.

Throw in the extremely high price tag, and I’ve always suspected that a significant number of iPhone Duo buyers would be viewing it as an experiment rather than a committed purchase. Our own Ryan Christoffel is an example of that “try it and see” attitude. One week in, he’s reached an interim conclusion that it’s probably not for him.

For those who’ve decided to return it, a number of readers shared their reasons.

“Returned it – I can’t go back to Touch ID.”

“I want to like it, but I just can’t get there. It’s awkward, and the outside screen is way too small.”

“Returned it. Not for me. I do not want to open the phone every time I want a larger screen and Apple made the outer display much less usable than it should be with that silly permanent dock. I also use my phones left-handed.”

“During a vacation in Morocco, we spent a night camping in the Sahara Desert. I was extremely careful with the phone and tried to avoid using it in the sand altogether. However, on the second day, when I opened it inside the tent, I heard a crunching sound coming from the hinge. Sand had somehow gotten inside. I tried everything I could to clean it, but nothing worked. The inner display was still functioning perfectly, but the phone would no longer open all the way. Even worse, when I tried to close it, I had to force it shut.”

For me personally, it couldn’t be my only phone, given the priority I place on the device as a camera, but I am still lusting after it. Given the continued extended delivery times – with random checks showing shipping in late January – I don’t think Apple has much to worry about here.

#3206. Speech Processing Pioneer Bishnu Saroop Atal Dies at 93

IEEE also bids farewell to innovators in space, power, and telecom

Bishnu Saroop Atal received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding.”

Bishnu Saroop AtalAcoustics and signal processing pioneerLife Fellow, 93; died 19 August

Atal was an acoustics and signal processing researcher at Bell Labs in Murray Hill, N.J., and later at AT&T’s Shannon Laboratory, in Florham Park, N.J. His pioneering work on voice-coding techniques became the foundation for efficient, high-quality voice transmission over cellular networks. He received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding.”

He joined Bell Labs in 1961 as a communications researcher, and his early work there focused on speaker identification technology. During the 1960s he helped develop linear predictive coding, a powerful method for analyzing and compressing speech. LPC is now the most widely used method for encoding speech at a low bit rate.

Atal developed increasingly sophisticated low-bit-rate speech-coding techniques. They included multipulse LPC, which improved the quality of compressed speech.

He also worked with his colleague Manfred R. Schroeder to develop code-excited linear prediction, a method for producing high-quality speech at very low bit rates. CELP became a foundational technique in modern speech coding, letting digital communications systems carry voice using less bandwidth. The extra efficiency expanded cellular capacity, allowing wireless networks to handle more simultaneous calls.

Later in his career, he led the acoustics and speech research departments at Bell.

The company named him a Fellow in 1994. When AT&T Bell Laboratories split into separate research organizations in 1996, Atal continued his career at the AT&T Florham Park headquarters, and he was named a Fellow the following year.

He retired in 2002 and became an affiliate professor of electrical engineering at the University of Washington, in Seattle. There he continued his research in speech processing, speech recognition, and high-dimensional computing.

Atal was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1987 and the National Academy of Sciences in 1993. He received numerous awards including the 2018 International Speech Communication Association Medal for Scientific Achievement and a 2003 medal from the Franklin Institute.

He received a bachelor’s degree in physics in 1952 from the University of Lucknow, in India, and a master’s degree in 1955 in electrical engineering from the Indian Institute of Science, in Bengaluru. While working full time at Bell he earned a Ph.D. in EE in 1968 from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn (now New York University’s Tandon engineering school), in New York City.

Darryl Palmer Jr.Chair of the IEEE Central Illinois SectionSenior member, 55; died 30 August

Palmer was a dedicated IEEE volunteer, serving as chair of the Central Illinois Section and as the government relations chair of Region 4. He was a member of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society and its industrial activity committee. He also served as associate editor of the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics.

In 1986, at age 16, Palmer completed a summer internship at NASA’s Glenn Research Center, in Cleveland. He helped develop FoilSim, an interactive educational software program that introduces aerodynamic engineering to preuniversity students.

While studying computer science at Cleveland State University in 1996, he joined the university’s Allen-Bradley PLC lab as a research assistant. He designed hardware and software systems for the Glenn Research Center to collect and process thermal wave imaging data. He also designed software for General Motors’ North American robotic and welding division.

In 1999 he completed a second internship at the research center and helped develop EngineSim, an educational software program that models jet engine design and testing.

For his work, NASA recognized him with a Space Act Award.

In 2000 he earned his bachelor’s degree in computer science and became a software engineer at the Danfoss Drives manufacturing facility in Loves Park, Ill. He worked on embedded control systems for variable-frequency drives and high-power equipment. He also developed sensorless control technology for beam pumps used in the oil and gas industry.

In 2014 Palmer and his wife, Alexandra “Sasha” Goodwin, founded Janus Choice, a health technology platform that matches hospital patients with post-acute care facilities. He served as its CEO until the company closed in 2020.

From 2018 to 2023, he was a lead software engineer at Adept Coalescence, a startup in Rockford, Ill., focused on developing front-end software for control systems. He then worked in Peoria, Ill., as a control systems team lead at Caterpillar, a manufacturer of construction and mining equipment.

Henry Leopold RichterTelecommunications engineerLife senior member, 99; died 12 August

Richter was a spacecraft engineer at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, in Pasadena, Calif., before starting his own public safety communications consultancy.

He earned a bachelor’s degree and a Ph.D. at Caltech in 1952 and 1956, respectively. In 1955 he joined JPL as an engineer and supervisor of its new circuit elements group. Later, he was assigned to NASA’s Explorer program as project manager for satellite design, serving as a liaison between the organization’s satellite instrumentation group and its operations and data groups. Since 1958 the program has launched more than 90 missions for physics, geophysics, and astrophysics research.

As NASA prepared to launch Explorer 1 in January 1958, Richter worked with the San Gabriel Valley Radio Club in Los Angeles to set up stations across the United States to track the satellite.

He eventually was named JPL section chief and was responsible for scientific instruments on the lunar Ranger, Surveyor, and Mariner programs. He also helped develop NASA’s Deep Space Network, an international tracking and communications system.

Richter left NASA to become vice president and technical director of Xerox Electro-Optical Systems, in Pasadena, Calif.

In the mid-1970s, he joined the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department as a communications engineer, overseeing the department’s microwave and mobile radio networks.

He later ran a telecommunications consulting practice for more than 20 years. His clients included federal, state, and local government agencies, school districts, universities, and organizations. His work covered strategic technology planning and the design and implementation of public safety radio, microwave, CCTV, and paging systems.

He wrote several books including America’s Leap Into Space: My Time at JPL and the First Explorer Satellites (2015), a personal account of his experience working on the Explorer 1 and America’s space program.

In 2019 the Radio Club of America presented him with its Lifetime Achievement Award for “significant achievements and a major body of work that has advanced the art and science of wireless technology.”

Raymond L. GiordanoFormer RCA engineerLife member, 91; died 19 July

Giordano was an electrical engineer who designed integrated circuits and defense electronics at companies including Harris, Intersil, and RCA.

After earning his bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering in 1956 from the Newark College of Engineering (now the New Jersey Institute of Technology), Giordano joined RCA in Moorestown, N.J., as an engineer. He helped develop a video formatter for the company’s missile and surface radar division, and he taught in-house engineering courses, eventually attaining the rank of senior technical staff member.

Later he developed technologies for General Electric (which acquired RCA in 1986), Intersil, and Harris. He designed the circuitry for Kodak’s Cameo cameras and one of its laser printers.

Giordano was awarded several patents for his designs including a smoke detector chip for Siemens, a speed control chip for Ford, an engine control system for Delco Remy, and a control component for Chrysler.

He earned a master’s degree in EE in 1964 from the University of Pennsylvania, in Philadelphia.

Delano D. WilsonPresident of Power TechnologiesLife Fellow, 92; died 26 May

Wilson was president and CEO of Power Technologies, a consulting firm in Schenectady, N.Y., that specialized in electric power systems.

He was a director of R&D at General Electric in Schenectady until he joined Power Technologies in 1974 as a principal engineer. He developed utility systems and software for the company.

Wilson authored six books and 65 technical papers, and he held two patents.

Outside of his engineering work, he served on the boards of several hospitals, YMCAs, Rotary clubs, and chambers of commerce.

After returning to his hometown of Great Falls, Mont., in 1995, he volunteered as a court-appointed advocate, a trained community volunteer appointed by a judge to represent the interests of children in foster care.

Daniel I. Amey Jr.Electronic packaging engineerLife Fellow, 84; died 12 March

Amey was an electronic packaging engineer, working at several companies including General Dynamics, Sperry Univac, and E.I. du Pont de Nemours (now DuPont). His research interests included connectors, chip packages, and high-frequency materials.

He began his career in 1963 as an engineer in the General Dynamics electronics division, where he designed military electronic hardware including analog and digital support equipment for aerospace applications.

In 1967 he joined Sperry Univac in Blue Bell, Pa. From 1972 to 1981 he was engineering manager of packaging techniques, responsible for interconnection hardware for small and medium computer systems. His work focused on large-scale integration packages, hybrid circuits, connectors, and printed wiring board processes.

He left the company to serve as director of electronics technology at Thomas & Betts of Raritan, N.J. He led research and development of packaging and interconnection products there.

In 1986 he became a director of Elco, an electrical component manufacturer in Huntingdon, Pa., where he was responsible for the design and development of connector and packaging hardware.

In 1988 he joined E.I. du Pont de Nemours as director of its electronics and communications technology group in Research Triangle Park, N.C. He worked on packaging technology development, high-frequency materials characterization, and applications engineering. He retired from there as a research fellow.

Amey wrote or cowrote more than 70 technical papers and held more than 14 patents. He developed courses on electronic packaging and printed wiring technology for education companies McGraw-Hill and Cobblestone (formerly the Center for Professional Advancement).

He received the International Microelectronics Assembly and Packaging Society’s 2004 Wagnon Technical Achievement Award and the Electronic Industries Association’s 1984 Distinguished Engineering Contribution Award.

After receiving a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering and a master’s degree in engineering science from Pennsylvania State University, he earned an MBA from Lehigh University, in Bethlehem, Pa.

Amanda Davis is a freelance writer based in San Diego.

#3205. Chipotle Mexican Grill vs. Coca-Cola: Which Stock Is a Buy After the Nvidia Sell-Off?

The better pick depends on whether you want growth or steady income.

As Nvidia (NVDA -4.34%) stock faces a sell-off, investors may be considering rotating into consumer good stocks for more protection. Two such companies that some may be considering are Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG -4.01%) and Coca-Cola (KO -0.13%).

Chipotle focuses on rapid domestic expansion to capture market share. Meanwhile, Coca-Cola leverages its vast bottling system to dominate international markets. Both represent significant players in their respective fields, but they offer distinct financial profiles for long-term investors.

Chipotle Mexican Grill operates a fleet of company-owned restaurants focused on a limited menu of fresh ingredients. By operating within the retail stocks segment, the company avoids the complexities of franchising and maintains more control over its brand experience. Third-party delivery services account for over 16% of food and beverage revenue, which highlights the importance of the digital ecosystem to its modern business strategy.

In its latest annual report, filed for FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $11.9 billion, representing growth of approximately 5.4% over the previous year. Net income for the period was close to $1.5 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 12.9%. While the company has faced rising input costs, its ability to maintain double-digit net margins indicates a high level of pricing power among its customer base.

Coca-Cola operates as a total beverage company, manufacturing concentrates and syrups that are sold to a global network of bottling partners. Its system reaches multiple countries and territories. The company also maintains a strategic relationship with Monster Beverage (MNST +0.37%) and is expanding its reach into energy drinks and dairy.

In FY 2025, revenue reached close to $47.9 billion, marking an increase of nearly 1.9% year over year. Net income for the fiscal year was approximately $13.1 billion, supporting a strong net margin of 27.3%. This level of profitability is characteristic of its asset-light model, where bottling partners handle much of the capital-intensive manufacturing and distribution work.

Chipotle Mexican Grill faces material risks from food safety incidents, which can rapidly damage brand reputation and sales across its thousands of locations. The company also operates in a highly competitive landscape against rivals like McDonald's (MCD -0.43%) and Starbucks (SBUX -2.39%). Furthermore, its aggressive growth strategy is sensitive to the availability of prime real estate and its ability to recruit and retain thousands of qualified employees.

Coca-Cola is exposed to risks from global economic conditions, including currency exchange rate fluctuations that can impact reported earnings. It must constantly innovate to meet changing consumer preferences regarding health and sugar content while competing with PepsiCo (PEP -1.17%) and Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP -7.40%). Additionally, the company faces ongoing tax litigation with the IRS and regulatory pressure regarding the environmental impact of plastic packaging.

Each stock looks similar with its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, while the bigger difference shows up in the price-to-sales (P/S) ratio.

These are both well-run companies, and they each benefit from consumer habits. The difference in the stocks for the longer term, however, comes down to what an investor is looking for in their portfolio.

The Coca-Cola stock price has done exceptionally well in 2026, with shares climbing nearly 40%. That said, the main reason to own Coca-Cola is its status as a consistent dividend payer, having increased that payout for 64 consecutive years. The key to owning the beverage maker as an income stock is whether those dividend payouts are likely to keep increasing, which, at least according to the 2026 third-quarter results, they are. For that third quarter, Coca-Cola shared it generated $11.4 billion in free cash flow for the first nine months of the year, boasting an operating margin of 33.4%. Revenue also increased 7%, with earnings per share growing 8% and operating income climbing 12%, providing plenty of flexibility to keep those dividend payouts and increases rolling in for shareholders.

In comparison, while a mature company in its own right, Chipotle is still more of a growth stock than Coca-Cola. In its third quarter, revenue increased by roughly 10%, customer transactions climbed, and it opened 84 new restaurants. It also has a long-term goal of opening 7,000 locations in North America.

Between the two, it comes down to whether an investor is looking for an income stream or the potential for greater stock price appreciation.

A proprietary transmission design carrying six times more power could reshape how utilities monetize grid upgrades for decades.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, American Electric Power (AEP -0.23%) introduced a $100 billion five-year capital plan to support expanding grid infrastructure and power demand. That massive spending commitment directly shapes the utility's earnings trajectory and customer rate structures through 2031. Three things management said stand out.

Proprietary transmission designs, binding long-term contracts, and constructive regulatory cost-recovery mechanisms support long-term revenue growth. Management is focusing on regulatory approvals, turbine procurement, and capital allocation discipline.

#3201. AMD plans to invest in PsiQuantum as they team up on quantum computers

The two will co-design the computing systems that run large quantum computers, starting with drug discovery. Neither PsiQuantum nor AMD has said how much AMD will invest.

AMD plans to invest in PsiQuantum, as the two expand their partnership on quantum computing. The companies announced the deal on 12 November. Neither said how much AMD will invest.

PsiQuantum already uses AMD’s Versal FPGAs to develop its fault-tolerant quantum computer. These are chips that engineers can reprogram after manufacture. The new deal adds AMD’s Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs and ROCm software. PsiQuantum brings its silicon photonics, which uses light to compute.

The two will co-design the infrastructure that runs large quantum computers. They will also build hybrid software that mixes quantum, high-performance and AI computing. They expect the result to be the world’s most powerful hybrid computing fabric, the companies said.

“Quantum computing will enable solving problems in healthcare, materials, energy, finance, and other domains that are out of reach today, working in concert with AI and high-performance computing,” said Victor Peng, PsiQuantum’s chief executive.

Working with AMD, PsiQuantum researchers have tuned PRISM, a machine-learning decoder, to run fast on programmable chips. Its job is to correct errors in real time in large photonic quantum computers. The companies linked a research paper on the work.

The first focus will be drug discovery. PsiQuantum runs its chemistry methods on AMD GPUs. The companies say this has already produced breakthrough results in simulations of covalent inhibitors, molecules relevant to cancer drug research.

The work fits the US Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis list of science problems for quantum computers, the companies said.

“We see that same opportunity with quantum computing, where leadership in classical computing is essential to building systems at scale,” said Mark Papermaster, AMD’s chief technology officer.

PsiQuantum is the anchor tenant of the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago. The two companies will look at working together there too. They plan to share more at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago, from 15 to 20 November.

In October, the Pentagon offered PsiQuantum a conditional $150m loan. The same month, AMD agreed to invest $1bn in Meta. Last week, it reported a record quarter.
